title: Mode A — server-embedded ingest and pointer-plus-snippet retrieval
background: US-43.1 gives the tier storage and no way to reach it. This story adds the HTTP surface for the mode where loopctl does the embedding: the client sends chunk text, loopctl embeds it with the corpus's pinned model, and corpus_search returns ranked pointers. Mode A is the right shape for material that is public anyway — HCPF companion guides, X12 Glass captures, published books — where there is nothing to protect and the keyword lane is worth having. The retrieval contract is the part that most needs holding: corpus_search returns {source_ref, locator, snippet, score, corpus_id} and deliberately does NOT return whole documents. The agent is told page 47 of a named file and opens it. That keeps responses small, keeps the loop honest about where truth lives, and is identical in both modes, which is what lets US-43.3 add mode B without a second retrieval contract.

story.as_a: an agent that needs to quote an authoritative reference document
story.i_want_to: index a corpus of verbatim chunks and search it, getting back a file pointer and a snippet
story.so_that: I can open the exact page of the exact document instead of trusting a summary or reading 1300 pages

rationale: Pointer-plus-snippet is the whole design in one contract. Returning bodies would make this a slower Knowledge Wiki with worse writing; returning only scores would make it unusable. The pointer keeps the file the source of truth, which is what makes the tier safe to point at a repo it does not own. Mode A ships first because it needs no client-side machinery, so the retrieval contract can be proven correct before US-43.3 removes the server's ability to read the text.

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /api/v1/corpora creates a corpus (mode server_embedded), GET /api/v1/corpora lists them, GET /api/v1/corpora/:id returns one with its status, DELETE /api/v1/corpora/:id deletes it. Role gates follow the CLAUDE.md checklist and are stated in each controller's moduledoc: create/list/status are role: :agent (non-destructive and audited), DELETE is role: :user (set-based blast radius AND irreversible — one call destroys every chunk and vector in the corpus and nothing restores them).

POST /api/v1/corpora/:id/index accepts a bounded batch of chunks, each {source_ref, locator, text, ordinal}, plus the optional top-level source_complete list AC-43.2.3 defines, and is role: :agent. The batch ceiling is ONE module attribute read by both the guard and the OpenAPI spec, so a caller can size its batches and the two cannot drift. loopctl computes content_hash server-side from the text — the client does not supply it in mode A — embeds the batch in ONE provider call, and writes every chunk and its embedding in ONE Ecto.Multi with per-item step names, committed once. This follows Loopctl.Embeddings.upsert_article_embeddings/3, whose per-item predecessor opened ~100 transactions against the 3-connection admin pool and had no atomicity, so a failure at item 60 left 59 rows written while the job re-ran and re-billed the provider for all 100 texts. Convergence on failure comes from the batch being bounded plus AC-43.2.3's idempotency, not from partial commits.

Indexing is IDEMPOTENT: a chunk row is KEYED by (corpus_id, source_ref, locator) — the unique index of US-43.1 AC-43.1.2 — and content_hash is the ordinary column that decides whether that row is rewritten. Re-submitting an unchanged batch performs no writes, spends no embedding tokens, and reports per-item {unchanged | inserted | replaced}. A chunk whose content_hash changed REPLACES the row at the same (corpus_id, source_ref, locator) and re-embeds. content_hash covers the TEXT, so it decides the EMBEDDING and not the whole write: snippet and ordinal are cast from the client and are in the upsert's replace list, so a chunk whose text held still while one of them moved is reported replaced and its row rewritten WITHOUT re-embedding — deciding both on the hash discarded a corrected snippet silently and left no later re-index able to apply it. Pruning is reconciliation over a source's COMPLETE chunk set, so it is never inferred from a batch: the request names source_complete for the sources it is reconciling, and only those are touched — a source_ref whose chunk set shrank then has its surplus chunks deleted, so a document that lost a page does not keep serving it. A name DECLARES that source's complete chunk set, in one of two forms: a bare source_ref string, whose complete set is what this request carries for it; or {source_ref, locators}, whose complete set is the declared locator manifest. The manifest form is what makes a document larger than the batch ceiling reconcilable at all: a large document split across several bounded batches names the source WITH its manifest only on the batch that completes it, and every chunk the manifest declares is kept, so batch three never deletes the chunks batches one and two wrote. The batch_too_large message states that same rule, and the response reports the prune PER NAMED SOURCE (meta.pruned_by_source) rather than folding it into one aggregate, so what each name cost is visible; the audit entry records the same map, because this is the one index verb that destroys data. Three refusals keep the delete bounded and the verb below the :user line: a source_ref may be named ONLY if the same request carries at least one chunk for it; a manifest may not omit a locator the same request carries, which would write a chunk and delete it in one transaction; and a BARE name may not delete more chunks than the request carries for that source, so one chunk of a 5,000-chunk source can never destroy the other 4,999 — a caller genuinely removing most of a document declares the surviving locators instead.

POST /api/v1/corpora/:id/search takes a query string, embeds it with the corpus's pinned model, and returns ranked results as {source_ref, locator, snippet, score, corpus_id, chunk_id} ordered by descending score. It NEVER returns the full chunk text — the snippet is bounded by one module attribute that the OpenAPI spec's maxLength and the enforcing truncation both read, so the documented bound and the enforced bound cannot drift.

Search runs both lanes in mode A — semantic over the per-dimension HNSW index, and keyword over the chunk text — fused by the SAME RRF the article path uses. That fuser is today Loopctl.Knowledge's private fuse_rrf/6, fixed at three lanes; its body keys only on result.id, so it is ALREADY lane-shape-agnostic and what blocks reuse is defp plus the fixed arity, not the shape. This story exposes it (public, or a lane-list arity) and has the corpus path call it with an empty graph lane, keeping one rrf_k (the :knowledge_rrf_k setting, default 60) and one tiebreak, rather than writing a second fuser that drifts. The article path's behaviour must not change and its existing fusion tests are the evidence. Scores stay rank-derived and comparable within a result set. The response's meta names which lanes ran, so a caller can tell a semantic-only result set from a fused one without inferring it.

GET /api/v1/corpora/:id/status reports per-source content hashes and chunk counts, so a client can index only what moved rather than resubmitting the corpus. The response is bounded and paginated; a corpus with thousands of sources does not return them all in one body.

Every mutating endpoint writes to the append-only audit log fail-closed, using Loopctl.Audit.log_in_multi/3 INSIDE the same Ecto.Multi as the mutation, so a failed audit rolls the write back; the transaction's error path returns {:error, :audit_write_failed}, which the FallbackController renders as a 500 carrying code audit_write_failed and never masks as a 404. Indexing and search are rate-limited per tenant via the per-endpoint plug idiom (see ChannelPostController), with the endpoint cap set BELOW the pipeline's per-key cap so the specific 429 stays the binding, observable constraint instead of being shadowed by an anonymous pipeline 429. The index limit is charged per ITEM, not per request, because one request may carry a large batch.

Every new endpoint carries an OpenApiSpex operation/2 spec declaring its parameters, its size caps, its 4xx codes and its role requirement. A new environment variable, if any is introduced (batch ceiling, snippet length, rate-limit window), gets a row in deploy/FLY_SECRETS.md with its default and what breaks if it is wrong — mix loopctl.check_env_docs runs in mix precommit and fails the build otherwise.

A tenant with no configured embedding credential gets a named 422 at corpus_create time in mode A, not a failure at first index. The error states that mode A embeds server-side on the tenant's own key and names the one call that provisions it, matching the BYO remediation shape the ingestion endpoint already uses. Creation also rejects a mode A corpus whose declared dim disagrees with Loopctl.Embeddings.Dimensions.for_model/1's native dimension for the model — the one model failure the server can detect without a provider call. An UNKNOWN model is NOT rejected: for_model/1 returns nil outside its curated table and the article path reads nil as cannot-check rather than invalid (pin_set/2's nil clause), so refusing it here would block a fine-tuned or locally-named model that embeds fine. Whether the tenant's endpoint actually SERVES the named model is not knowable server-side and stays a first-index failure; the criterion does not claim otherwise.

Search is a heavy read: it goes through Loopctl.HeavyRead with a tagged endpoint, inherits the per-read SET LOCAL statement_timeout, and degrades on overload the way semantic article search does — returning a tagged error the caller maps to keyword-only rather than raising a 429 through to the agent.

The corpus search endpoint is REGISTERED in all FOUR places a heavy ANN read must appear: Loopctl.HeavyRead's @known_endpoints, which is the source of truth the other three are checked against — heavy_read_hnsw_ef_search_test.exs asserts ann_endpoints/0 is a subset of it, and heavy_read_guard_test.exs statically scans lib/ for every literal HeavyRead.opts(:endpoint) atom against it, so registering only the others fails both tests; Loopctl.HeavyRead's @ann_endpoints, without which it gets no SET LOCAL hnsw.ef_search and the HNSW scan returns pgvector's default breadth regardless of how large a pool the code asks for; TenantGate's @heavy_endpoints, without which it is admitted at the wrong cost weight and cannot be shed under load; and the @expected_weights map in test/loopctl/heavy_read/tenant_gate_test.exs, which asserts MapSet equality against known_endpoints/0 and so fails deterministically until the endpoint carries a deliberate heavy/light weight decision. A test asserts the endpoint atom appears in all four.

The new routes are declared with every LITERAL path before any parameterized sibling (the router invariant stated in comments throughout the knowledge block), and a new OpenAPI tag is added to Loopctl.ApiSpec's tags list so the endpoints are grouped rather than untagged.

The routes are added to LoopctlWeb.RouteDiscoveryController's hand-curated curated_routes/0 AND a /api/v1/corpora arm is added to test/loopctl_web/controllers/route_discovery_controller_test.exs alongside the existing /api/v1/admin and /api/v1/channel arms. Only the index-to-router direction is universal there; the router-to-index direction is filtered to those two prefixes, so WITHOUT a corpora arm an omitted route fails nothing and the surface ships undiscoverable via GET /api/v1/routes. The new arm carries the same non-empty-filter assertion the other two do, so it cannot go vacuous if the route shape drifts.

test_cases.name: re-indexing an unchanged corpus is a no-op
preconditions: a mode A corpus with 50 indexed chunks
expected_results: every item reports unchanged
no embedding call is made
chunk and embedding row counts are unchanged
updated_at on the chunks is unchanged

test_cases.name: a changed document replaces only its own chunks
preconditions: a corpus with chunks from two source_refs
steps: resubmit one source_ref with altered text for one chunk
expected_results: that chunk is replaced and re-embedded
the other chunks of that source are unchanged
the other source_ref is untouched

test_cases.name: a document that lost chunks stops serving them
steps: resubmit that source_ref with 7 chunks WITHOUT naming it in source_complete
resubmit the same 7 chunks, naming it in source_complete
expected_results: 3 chunks are deleted
their embeddings are deleted
search never returns the removed locators
a batch that does NOT name the source in source_complete deletes nothing

test_cases.name: search returns pointers and never bodies
preconditions: a corpus with a chunk whose text is far longer than the snippet bound
steps: search for a phrase in that chunk
expected_results: the result carries source_ref, locator, a snippet at or under the bound, a score and ids
no field in the response contains the full chunk text

test_cases.name: the documented snippet bound equals the enforced one
preconditions: the controller module attribute and its operation/2 spec
steps: read the maxLength from the generated OpenAPI spec
read the truncation bound applied at runtime
expected_results: they are the same value and both derive from one attribute

test_cases.name: delete requires a user key
preconditions: an agent-role key and a user-role key in the same tenant
steps: DELETE the corpus with the agent key
expected_results: the agent key is refused with insufficient_role
the user key succeeds
chunks and embeddings are gone

test_cases.name: a failed batch leaves nothing behind and a retry converges
preconditions: a batch of 10 chunks where embedding fails on the 6th
expected_results: no chunk from the batch is persisted
no embedding row is persisted
the error names the failing item
resubmitting the corrected batch persists all 10

test_cases.name: tenant isolation on search
preconditions: tenant A and tenant B each with a corpus containing a distinctive phrase
steps: as tenant A, search for tenant B's phrase
expected_results: zero results
no cross-tenant chunk id appears in any field

test_cases.name: index rate limit is charged per item
preconditions: a tenant near its index rate limit
steps: submit one request carrying a large batch
expected_results: the limit is charged once per item, not once per request
the ceiling is reached at the item count, not the request count

test_cases.name: an audit write failure fails the request
preconditions: a corpus and an audit path stubbed to fail
expected_results: the request fails
no chunk is persisted
the failure is distinguishable from a validation error

technical_notes: Reuse the retrieval machinery rather than writing a second one. The candidate-pool shape in Loopctl.Knowledge.VectorSearch exists because applying selective filters on the index-ordered scan flipped the planner off HNSW at production scale (the #170/#172 shape, verified by EXPLAIN at 80k articles). A corpus search filtered by corpus_id has exactly the same hazard, so filter on the OUTER over-the-pool subquery, not on the inner ANN.

corpus_id is a selective filter and a corpus is usually a small fraction of a tenant's chunks, which is the case where an ANN pool can come back empty after filtering. Size the pool against the corpus, or scope the ANN by corpus in a way that stays index-safe, and test the case where the target corpus is a small minority of the tenant's chunk rows. This is the most likely source of a silently-empty search.

The keyword lane needs a search_vector generated column over document_chunks.text plus its GIN index, and this story owns both — US-43.1 creates the table and deliberately leaves the FTS column here. A generated column cannot read config at runtime, so bake Regconfig.get() in at migration time and bind the SAME regconfig at the query site, as Loopctl.Knowledge does for articles. Do not promise the two lanes can never disagree: 20260724190000_apply_fts_regconfig.exs does NOT re-run when FTS_REGCONFIG changes later, so on such a deployment article and corpus vectors can carry different stemmers and rebuilding is a deliberate operator action, out of scope here.

Do NOT reuse Loopctl.Embeddings.active_dimension/1 anywhere in this story. The corpus's own dim is authoritative (US-43.1). A single call to the tenant resolver is the defect this epic exists to avoid, and it will look correct.

corpus_search must NOT be added to /api/v1/recall, and this is worth stating in the controller moduledoc rather than only in the epic README. The recall hook injects into every repo's session; verbatim spec chunks there would be the pollution the separate table exists to prevent.

An over-long chunk is a real case for a verbatim tier — a page of dense EDI tables can exceed the provider's input limit. Loopctl.Embeddings.ShrinkLadder already handles it and its contract must be honoured: a shrunk vector returns {:ok, vector, :truncated} rather than a bare {:ok, vector}, and the truncation is marked in the content hash via truncated_hash/1, because a prefix vector is not comparable with whole-text vectors. Do not silently truncate; a chunk whose vector covers only its first half must be distinguishable, or re-indexing will read it as unchanged forever.

The batch embed path takes ONE admission token for the whole array, and vectors must be mapped back by the provider response's index field NEVER by array position, with a partial response failing the whole batch. That is the EmbeddingBehaviour contract; reuse it rather than writing a second client.

Mode A embedding is mandatory-BYO like every other embedding path: the client resolves the tenant's own key and a keyless tenant makes ZERO provider calls. That is what AC-43.2.9 moves earlier, to corpus_create, so the failure is not discovered at first index.
